bunkhouse.note: A new class = one Farmer Generator export + a stat block + one ability. Show locked ones as dark silhouettes.

seedCatalog.startingWeaponNote: Named for the same reason the items are. The slice took the first eight keys of weapons.json, which are the six firearms plus the Chem Sprayer and the Bait Drum -- so a fresh save could not be offered a single MELEE weapon, and the two classes whose whole identity is standing and swinging opened into a pool with nothing for them. The named eight are a spread: two guns, two blades, a thrown, a sprayer, a hammer and the Smudge Pot. Everything else is still bought at the catalog.
seedCatalog.startingItemNote: The opening pool, named rather than sliced. It USED to be `Object.keys(ITEMS).slice(0, 12)` -- the first twelve keys of items.json in authoring order -- and eleven of those twelve are the common stat cards. So a fresh save's entire item pool was the eleven percentages, and every board the player saw for the first several hours was four of them: exactly the complaint docs/UPGRADE_ROSTER.md exists to answer, invisible to both harnesses because neither calls setUnlocked. A real run photographed it (tools/play/batch1) after the rebuild had already measured clean. Ten commons stay -- they are the teaching set and they should be -- and six cards that DO something join them: a pierce, two on-kill cards, a reflect, and two Loads, so the first shop is a real decision and the first level-up board is not four percentages. Everything else is still bought at the catalog. A card named here that does not exist is skipped, so this list cannot break a rename silently.
seedCatalog.note: Unlocks are permanent and enter every future run's pool. Makes runs wider, not stronger.
